segments.text: Imagine you run a massive jungle delivery business.
Some days you need to translate complex ancient maps.
Other days you just need to sort mail or organize banana baskets.
For all of this, open AI gave us three different monkey helpers
in their GPT 5.6 family.
Soul, Terra, and Luna.
They all share the exact same memory size
but their brain power and banana cost are completely different.
Let's start with Luna, the skied racer.
Luna is like a tiny chimpanzee on a skateboard.
She is lightning fast and works for almost pennies.
If you need her to quickly categorize incoming emails or detect simple spam,
Luna is your go-to.
But don't ask her to solve a complex coding puzzle.
She'll get confused and drop the ball.
Next is Terra, the balanced worker.
Think of Terra as your reliable everyday assistant monkey.
Terra is smart enough to handle regular agent workflows,
write standard emails and draft simple blog posts.
She is the middle ground, giving you solid reasoning
without costing too many bananas.
Finally, we have Soul, the grand chieftain of the jungle.
Soul is the heavy lifting gorilla who sits on a throne of books.
Soul is expensive and takes a bit longer to think
but has massive reasoning power.
If you need to audit security code, design a database,
or solve complex logic riddles,
Soul is the only one who can do it.
Why not just use Soul for everything?
Because you'll run out of bananas in minutes.
And why not use Luna for everything?
Because she isn't smart enough for complex tasks.
Choosing the right tier is all about matching the job to the right brain power.
So, are you building a high speed chat widget,
a standard automated agent, or a deep analysis tool?
Pick the right monkey helper, save your bananas, and build something awesome.
